A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Equivariant Splitting work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction experiments on compressive sensing, inpainting, MRI, and CT in Section 5, with additional empirical analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains these original reconstruction experiments and the appendix ablations, robustness tests, and empirical equivariance validation.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same ES loss, noisy-measurement variant, equivariant architectures, and training and inference procedures, including Algorithms 1-2.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, DIV2K, FastMRI, and LIDC-IDRI with the same tasks. Real MRI, noise-dominated MRI, push-broom inpainting, and unknown-noise scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: supervised reconstruction, EI, MC/SURE, and the applicable learning-free baselines. The pseudo-inverse comparison in Figure 4 and comparator rows in appendix tables are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same data splits, masks, acceleration factors, noise levels, preprocessing, architectures, and PSNR/SSIM/EQUIV metrics. Training budgets in Table 10 are identical.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations, training curves, nearly equivariant push-broom operator test, unknown-noise robustness analysis, and MAP-equivariance validation are unchanged. Their relocation introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and sampling information. No seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All matched tables and figure results are unchanged. For example, synthetic MRI at eightfold acceleration retains ES PSNR 28.54 ± 2.75 and EI 27.88 ± 2.64 in v4 Table 1 and v5 Table 2. Appendix scores and qualitative reconstructions are also identical.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Definition 1, Theorems 1-3, Proposition 1, Corollary 1, and the appendix lemma retain their mathematical content. Appendix C proofs are identical after accounting for pagination.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reconstruction equivariance, the ES loss and its MMSE guarantees under stated conditions, and competitive reconstruction performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of learned equivariance, computational efficiency, noise robustness, and failure with nearly equivariant operators are retained. Appendix discussions of transformation suitability and averaging costs also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New acknowledgements identify GENCI/IDRIS resources on Jean Zay's H100 partition and computations at the Pascal Blaise Center cluster. This adds computing-resource provenance; existing hyperparameters, training durations, and the code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Quemener and Corvellec (2013), cited in the computing-resource acknowledgements. The remaining references, related-work discussion, and scientific novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds Section 7, Acknowledgements, and moves the reproducibility statement from after the conclusion to after Appendix C, adding a pointer to the existing code disclosure. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays are repositioned with revised spacing. Medical and inpainting tables exchange numbers 1/2, while noisy-MRI and transformation-selection tables exchange 4/5. Figure 1 moves beside Section 5.1, and the noisy-MRI table moves from Appendix A to B.4. Display designs and contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves navigation by placing medical results after their experimental descriptions and moving the noisy-MRI table from the method appendix to Appendix B.4. Computing-resource acknowledgements add limited transparency. These presentation and disclosure gains improve readability without changing the scientific evidence or theoretical support.
